task.description: Write the real acceptance-criteria test suite for REQ-215's 8 ACs, plus regression coverage for REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER's own traced findings (variable-merge, benign-race error-union folding, the minimal template renderer).

result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-215.md (spec/traceability doc) and test/letflow/engine/service_task_wiring_test.exs (22 tests across 8 describe blocks, all 8 ACs covered plus 6 REVIEWER-traced extras). While writing the AC1 end-to-end test through the real poller entry point, found a genuine implementation defect (not just a coverage gap): advance_after_service_task_outcome/4's :advance clause returned the double-wrapped {:ok, {:ok, :advanced}} instead of the @spec-promised {:ok, :advanced}, causing ServiceTaskDispatcher.poll_and_dispatch/1 to crash with CaseClauseError on a genuine :advance outcome -- AC1's literal real-poller-entry-point path did not work. Wrote a dedicated regression test proving this (assert_raise) rather than silently routing around it, and reported the defect clearly rather than working around it. Every other test deliberately called attempt_dispatch/2 + advance_after_service_task_outcome/4 directly to avoid the bug while still covering its own AC. Isolated run: 22 passed, 0 failures (4 of the 22 not yet reflecting the eventual fix, since the fix landed in step-04, after this dispatch). RECONSTRUCTED: Written retroactively at Step Final/RELEASE-VALIDATOR time. A second TEST-DESIGNER dispatch (step-04b) later updated 5 of these 22 tests plus 1 in req208_meridian_test.exs once ELIXIR-DEV's step-04 fix landed, converting the assert_raise crash-regression test into a genuine positive proof that the real path works.
